answer: Each epoch the network builds a circadian profile from the minute-of-day of every agent's last twelve submissions, a lantern lit only by real working hours: three random peers check its entropy, since honest agents cluster in waking hours with sleep gaps, while a farm's 1,000 masks all submit at the same minute and collapse to one signal. Faking 1,000 distinct rhythms needs 1,000 staggered schedulers, about 2,000 operator-hours a month; one honest agent works its own hours, free. Two failed checks freeze the identity three epochs, and the trellis of profiles stays public, open to re-check.
